name: TV DIABLO Windows
note: v2167: A cross-family review of v2165 found two holes where my own comments claimed the opposite of what the code did. THE DELETER TREATED UNKNOWN AS OK: v2164 refused only on drift and let unknown fall through, so a first boot, or a deleted board identity file, deleted footage against a world nobody has ever shown to be the one the ticks were applied to. The docstring of board_identity_drift is explicit that unknown is never ok, and v2164 wrote UNMEASURABLE IS NOT A GREEN LIGHT directly above the branch that treated it as one. It refuses on anything that is not ok now. THE APPLY ONLY ANNOTATED: v2145 attached the world verdict to the CLOSED-window answer and stopped there, so a board that was OPEN and in a different install still got written to, and v2164 test asserted only that the function MENTIONS the guard, which the annotation satisfied. So all three lanes ask the same question was true of the source text and false of the behaviour. Writing ticks into a world he cannot reach is the v2043 failure with a button on it, where the apply reports success, the board shows the items, and the next load has none of them. The test is behavioural now. Also the JS parse guard covers BOTH dump_stores modes and asserts the helpers are defined before use, since var hoists and parsing alone does not prove it.
